1081-u0-required-courses-27-credits: The first year of the 136- or 137-credit four-year program.
1081-u0-complementary-courses-6-or-7-cre: One calculus course and a 3-credit elective, then you enter U1.
1081-program-description: Online or on campus; register in the courses for the mode you were admitted to. See the School's B.N.I. page and p. 1078.
1083-school-of-physical-and-occupational: On McGill's upper campus: educates rehabilitation professionals, and researches how to improve health, function and participation.
1083-occupational-therapy: Uses occupation as therapy to improve health-related quality of life for people with injury, disability or psychosocial problems, from infancy to old age. In mental health, it helps clarify functional diagnosis and supports coping and community life. See the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists.
1083-physical-therapy: An autonomous, primary care profession that improves function, prevents and manages pain and impairment, and promotes fitness. Uses exercise, modalities, manual therapy, devices and lifestyle changes, in clinics, industry and the community.
1093-mcgill-alumnae-society-prize: At graduation, for excellence and high standing, preferring women.
1093-patricia-ann-macdonald-wells-van-da: Since 2003, for professional program students or Rehabilitation Science master's students, for a project on aging or clinical education.
1093-women-associates-of-mcgill-scholars: On high standing, after a year of the B.Sc., preferring women.
1093-continuing-students: Up to the top 10% in each faculty make the Dean's Honour List, on combined Fall and Winter GPA. No money, but on your transcript.
1093-graduating-students: Dean's Honour List with at least 60 McGill credits and a CGPA in your faculty's top 10%. All awards are in the Calendars.
1094-degree-requirements-for-the-b-sc-re: 90 credits, all courses passed, Satisfactory Standing and a curriculum CGPA of 2.3. Full-time because courses are sequential. Rules may change, generally not mid-year.
Promotion periods: U1 and U2, September to end of August; U3, September to end of April.
1094-admission-requirements-for-the-m-sc: Practice requires the M.Sc.A. in the same discipline. With CGPA 3.0+ you may be considered, starting in Summer after graduating, but it isn't guaranteed: three or more performance flags, or insufficient progress on skills, may block you.
Without this B.Sc., apply through a graduate Qualifying Year, or do the B.Sc. first.
1094-course-change-and-withdrawal-policy: See pp. 34. Programs are structured, so the Program Director approves changes. OCC1, PHTH and POTH courses are only for the School's students; leaving the program means leaving them.

You must start any withdrawal yourself in Minerva; telling instructors or stopping attendance doesn't count. After add/drop, drop complementary or elective courses by the deadline, or a missed exam gives J, which counts as zero permanently.
After the no-refund deadline, only in exceptional cases and not for poor work, you get W or WF, outside your GPA. If Minerva blocks an approved drop, get forms from Student Affairs.
1095-university-withdrawal: See p. 40, and talk to the Program Director and Student Affairs first. If you registered but won't attend, you must drop within deadlines.
If required to withdraw, or if you abandon studies, the School proceeds and you can't be readmitted to either program. It may dismiss anyone judged incompetent or unsuitable at any time.
1095-credit-system-for-physical-and-occu: The letter grade is official, and class averages show on transcripts. See pp. 52–53 and the Rules and Regulations.
1095-satisfactory-unsatisfactory-option: Can't be used for required courses, so normally not available.
1095-final-examinations: No mark is final until the Promotions and Review Committee (OTPRC or PTPRC) approves it and it's on your transcript; grades then appear in Minerva. See also pp. 22, 1002.
1095-interim-class-tests-and-mid-term-ex: Requirements are given by the end of week one. No in-term tasks in the last 10 working days, except take-homes given 15+ working days before classes end, and tasks worth 10% or less. Missing midterms, labs or interprofessional sessions needs the Program Director's approval, possibly with documents.
1096-supplemental-examinations: With committee permission, after a failure. OCC1, PHTH and POTH: timed by the instructor, within 30 days of grades if feasible, or official periods. Campus courses: March and August. Apply in Minerva. Both marks count in your GPA.
1096-deferred-examinations: For serious reasons, with the Program Director's permission, at the next deferred period. Apply in Minerva, tell Student Affairs quickly, and send documents within a week. No supplemental after failing a deferred exam: re-register or substitute with committee permission.
1096-inter-university-transfer-iut-and-t: Needs the Program Director's approval first. Courses must match in content and evaluation, per the Course Equivalency System, without overlaps. See p. 39 and Student Affairs. Exchanges: see Rules and Regulations.

The host's letter grade rules and must meet program minimums, but stays off your transcript and GPA. To drop, use the host's method and update the IUT application. Outside Quebec, have an official transcript sent to Student Affairs; late ones move you to the next graduation.
1096-physical-and-occupational-therapy-s: The OTPRC and PTPRC review records, conduct and performance, with final say on suitability, promotion and graduation. Read all program documents, updated yearly: Important Information, Rules and Regulations, Curriculum, Code of Conduct, and Required Skills and Attributes.
Full-time unless the committee allows part-time in writing. Only Minerva grades are official, not myCourses. Finish each promotion period before the next; at most one repeat.
C+ minimum in OCC1, PHTH and POTH, passing every component (individual, group, theory, practical). C for anatomy, physiology, complementaries and electives.
1097-student-athletes: See Important Information for Students for inter-university athletes and Sports Practicum students.
1097-probation-withdrawal-or-dismissal-f: Failures or unprofessional conduct trigger a full review. Probation: CGPA under 3.0, a failed requirement, or an integrity or conduct incident, with monitoring and possibly remedial work.

Unsatisfactory, requiring withdrawal: CGPA under 2.30 (B.Sc.) or 2.7 (M.Sc.A. and Qualifying Year), two or more failed courses including a repeat, or a second incident. No readmission to either program.
Plagiarism, cheating and misconduct can mean dismissal; criminal activity goes to the committee and may show unsuitability. Leaving voluntarily removes you from program courses.
1098-student-advising-in-physical-and-oc: See p. 1089, or contact the School.
1098-related-services: See pp. 79, 81. Ask an Advisor directs any undergraduate to the right place.
1098-the-wellness-hub: Awareness, prevention and early intervention, with a Local Wellness Advisor for this School.
1098-campus-life-and-engagement-new-stud: Helps new students with the catalogue and new-student site, with workshops, advice and referrals.
1098-career-planning-service-caps: Career advising, workshops, events and resources through graduation.
1098-becoming-a-licensed-occupational-or: The bachelor's gives access to the professional master's in the same field.
1098-licensing-regulations: M.Sc.A. graduates can seek licensure worldwide; each place sets its own exams, courses or TOEFL. Quebec needs a permit from the regulator and working French, spoken and written (p. 70).
OTs elsewhere in Canada pass a National Certification Exam. PTs elsewhere have needed the Physiotherapy National Exam or proof of Quebec licensing since 1993.
1098-canadian-national-offices: Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists: 2720 Queensview Dr., Unit 1142, Ottawa. Canadian Physiotherapy Association: 350 Sparks St., Suite 1209, Ottawa. Canadian Alliance of Physiotherapy Regulators: 1243 Islington Ave., Suite 501, Toronto.
1099-quebec-provincial-offices: Ordre des ergothérapeutes du Québec: 2021 avenue Union, bureau 920, Montréal. Ordre professionnel de la physiothérapie du Québec: 7151 rue Jean-Talon est, bureau 700, Anjou.
1099-international-offices: Check each country's or state's requirements.
1099-clinical-placement-requirements-fre: Clinical hours for membership are in the master's programs. Quebec's health system runs in French under the Charter, even at bilingual sites, so you need oral and written French for placements, at the level in the admission guides, before clinical work. Without it, placements are limited and graduation may be delayed. Keep CPR/AED at Health Care Provider level throughout.
1099-vaccinations: Finish before clinical courses, and start early, as schedules take months. Upload to the Wellness portal in September of U3 or Qualifying Year; the Hub must mark it Complete by March 1, for the M1 Summer term's two clinical courses. The Hub keeps your details confidential from the School.
1100-physical-and-occupational-therapy-p: Bachelor's in Rehabilitation Science lead to the M.Sc.A. The School stresses client-centred, evidence-based practice, clinical reasoning, ethics, teamwork and professionalism.
1100-admission-requirements-for-undergra: 90 credits, leading to the M.Sc.A. required for practice. McGill Admissions handles it: Service Point, 3415 McTavish St. See also Casper and French requirements. Those required to withdraw can't be readmitted.

Quebec DCS prerequisites: Biology 00UK, 00XU, 01Y5, 01YJ, NYA; Chemistry 00UL, 00UM, 00XV, 01Y6, 01YH, NYA, NYB; Math 00UN, 00UP, 01Y1, 01Y2, NYA, NYB; Physics 00UR, 00US, 00UT, 01Y7, 01YF, 01YG, NYA, NYB, NYC. Plus Casper and French proof.

After a year of college or university: two terms each of biology, general chemistry and physics, and one of organic chemistry, all with labs, plus differential and integral calculus, Casper and French. UK, Commonwealth, French Baccalaureate and IB: see Admissions.
1100-mcgill-inter-faculty-transfer: At least 24 McGill credits, with two terms each of biology and general chemistry, one of organic, two of physics (or three at CEGEP) with labs, two of calculus, Casper and French.
Out-of-Quebec high school graduates in 120-credit Science need these too. With under 24 credits, or a degree by August 1, apply through Enrolment Services instead.
